transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, um, thanks for seeing me. I guess I'm here because my head just won't give me a break lately, and it's just getting really exhausting. See, I drive a taxi—I got the job right out of high school, and it's a lot of responsibility, which I take really seriously. We have this whole safety check we have to do before every single shift. And I do it. I know I do it, I physically walk around the car and check the tires, the lights, everything. But man, even when I know for an absolute fact I did my safety check, this thought just keeps hitting me out of nowhere that I missed something on the cab. 

It just drops on me like a ton of bricks. My brain starts going, what if you didn't look close enough? What if something is loose? And I get so worked up thinking somebody could get hurt, like really hurt or get into a terrible accident because of me, or my boss is gonna look at the logs and say I lied about doing the inspection and fire me. I try to push it away and tell myself it's fine, but I just can't make it shut up. It's constantly playing on a loop the entire time I'm driving people around, which makes work so hard, and even when I'm off the clock and just sitting at home trying to study, I can't even read a single page. I just sit there staring at my books because the thought is so loud and I'm just so terrified I missed something on the car. It's just completely taking over everything I do.

When these thoughts come up about possibly missing something on the car, do you feel driven to do something over and over again, like checking the car again or mentally reviewing the check, to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, it's not just a passing thought where I go, "Oh, did I check that?" and then move on. It's like... it's like this overwhelming pressure that I *have* to make sure. So, before I can even accept a ride on the app, I end up getting out of the car again. And it's not just a quick walk-around. I start at the front left tire, and I kick it, then I check the headlight, then I check the driver's side door, make sure it latches exactly right. Then I check the meter, make sure the display is perfectly clear, and I go through all my paperwork in the glovebox. 

And the thing is, I'll do that whole circuit, right? But then I'll get back in the driver's seat, and my brain will say, "Wait, did you actually check the right rear tire, or did you just imagine you did?" So I have to get out and do it all over again. Sometimes I even take pictures of the tires and the lights with my phone, just so I have proof, but even looking at the pictures doesn't always help because what if the picture is blurry or what if something broke right after I took it? 

If the whole routine doesn't feel exactly right, if I get interrupted or if I just have this nagging feeling that it wasn't a "good" check, I have to start from the very beginning. I've done this... I don't even know how many times in a row. It's gotten to the point where passengers are literally standing on the curb waiting for me, looking at me like I'm crazy because I'm just circling the cab over and over. I've been late picking people up, I've been late starting my shift, all because I just can't stop checking. I just can't drive away until it feels perfect, and it almost never feels perfect.
